Surah 98 (Al-Bayyinah): It is Madani.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1} He, the Exalted, says: {Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture (ahl al-kitab) and the polytheists were not going to desist} — i.e., the Jews and the Christians, and {the polytheists}: from all the other kinds of nations — {[they were not] to desist from their disbelief and misguidance in which they were}; i.e., they would continue in their error and misguidance, and the passing of time would only increase them in disbelief, {until there came to them the clear evidence}: the manifest proof and the shining demonstration.

{2–3} Then he explained that clear evidence, saying: {A messenger from Allah}; i.e., Allah sent him to call people to the truth, and He revealed to him a Book that he recites, to teach people wisdom, purify them, and bring them out from darknesses into light. Hence He said: {reciting purified scriptures}; i.e., protected from the approach of devils, touched only by the purified, because they are the highest of speech. Hence He said concerning them: {therein}; i.e., in those scriptures, {are correct writings}; i.e., truthful reports and just commands guiding to the truth and to the straight path. So when this clear evidence comes to them, the seeker of truth is distinguished from one who has no aim in his seeking, so whoever perishes perishes after clear evidence, and whoever lives lives after clear evidence.

{4} And if the People of the Scripture did not believe in this Messenger and submit to him, this is no novelty in their misguidance and obstinacy, for they did not split, differ, and become factions {except after the clear evidence came to them}, which necessitates for its people gathering and agreement. But because of their baseness and meanness, guidance increased them only in misguidance, and insight only in blindness.

{5} Although all the Books came with one principle and one religion, they were commanded in all the laws only to worship {Allah, being sincere to Him in religion}; i.e., directing all their outward and inward acts of worship toward the face of Allah and seeking nearness to Him, {inclining}; i.e., turning away from and leaning away from all the religions that oppose the religion of monotheism. He singled out prayer and zakah for mention, although they are included in His saying {to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion}, because of their excellence and nobility and because they are the two acts of worship whereby one who establishes them establishes all the laws of the religion. {That}; i.e., monotheism and sincerity in religion, {is the upright religion}; i.e., the straight religion that leads to the gardens of bliss, and whatever else is other than it are paths leading to Hellfire.

{6} Then He mentioned the recompense of the disbelievers after the clear evidence had come to them, saying: {Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell}, its punishment having encompassed them and its retribution having intensified upon them, {abiding therein eternally}: its punishment will not be lightened for them, and they will be in it despairing. {Those are the worst of creatures}: because they knew the truth and abandoned it, and lost both this world and the Hereafter.

{7} {Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — those are the best of creatures}: because they worshipped Allah and knew Him, and succeeded with the bliss of this world and the Hereafter.

{8} {Their recompense with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence}; i.e., gardens of settlement in which there is no departure, no removal, and no seeking of any goal beyond them, {beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him}: He is pleased with them for what they performed of His pleasing acts, and they are pleased with Him for what He has prepared for them of various kinds of honours [and abundant rewards]. {That}: the good recompense, {is for those who fear their Lord}; i.e., for whoever fears Allah and refrains from His disobedience and performs what He has obligated upon him.

Completed. And praise be to Allah.
